newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING SAYS HIDDEN RESERVES DFL 2.55 BLN.
newsitem.headline: ING SAYS HIDDEN RESERVES DFL 2.55 BLN.

text.p: Financial services group ING Groep NV (ING) said on Thursday it had hidden reserves of 2.55 billion guilders at December 31.
ING was revealing for the first time the size of its provision for general contingencies, designated by the Dutch acronym VAR.
Analysts had forecast ING's VAR, or hidden reserves, at between 2.50 billion and 3.00 billion guilders.
Dutch banks have been ordered to unveil their VARs by the year 2000 to comply with changes to European Union rules.

ING said 1.25 billion guilders of the reserves would be transferred to shareholders equity with the balance going to the FAR, a new open fund designed for unexpected loan losses, potential claims and law suits. Under normal circumstances, no deductions will be made from this fund.
Actual loan losses, which were previously covered by additions to the VAR fund, will from 1997 be deducted directly from the bank's profit and loss account.
Analysts expect a one-off rise in Dutch bank profits as a result of these changes as banks overprovided for loan losses in the past and such provisions will fall in future.
